‘I thought it was my last day, I might not make it out alive’
item.description:
It was around 9:45am. Workers were going about their usual duties at the factory when suddenly they heard their colleagues shouting. Workers began running in different directions. Within moments, the fire spread. Thick black smoke engulfed the area, plunging everything into darkness. This is how eyewitnesses described the fire at Unit-2 of Drug International Limited in the Cherag Ali area of Tongi, Gazipur.

The fire broke out at Unit-2 of the factory on Wednesday morning. After nearly four hours of efforts by the Fire Service, the army and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), the blaze was brought under control. However, no casualties were reported in the incident.

Worker Ruma Akter was working on the factory's fourth floor. She told Prothom Alo, “I joined work this morning as usual. Suddenly, I saw smoke coming out. Within moments, the smoke spread across our floor. I and the other workers ran downstairs. While coming down, one of our colleagues lost consciousness. She was later rescued and taken outside. She is now well.”

When the fire broke out at the factory, workers started running in different directions. As smoke spread throughout the premises, everything became dark. They began making their way downstairs from wherever they were. This triggered panic among the workers.

Afroza Begum, a worker at the factory, told Prothom Alo, “When the smoke spread, I thought it was my last day. I might not make it out alive. Everything had gone dark. My eyes were burning because of the smoke. Only Allah knows how I managed to get out.”

Muslima Akter, a worker in the tablet section of the factory, described a similar experience. She said, “Two people were working behind me and two in front of me. Suddenly, someone behind us shouted that there was a fire. Then four or five of us got out. After coming out of the factory, I saw the fire raging.”

According to the Fire Service and factory workers, the fire spread rapidly to different parts of the building. The flames and smoke triggered panic in the surrounding areas. Medicines, production equipment and various materials inside the factory were reportedly being damaged by the fire.

After receiving news of the fire, 14 Fire Service units began working at the scene. Four more units later joined them. Eventually, a total of 21 Fire Service units from Gazipur, Tongi, Uttara and nearby areas worked together to bring the fire under control. Army personnel and members of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) joined the firefighting efforts around 1pm. At around 2pm, Brigadier General Sultanul Afreen Zunaid, director general of the Fire Service and Civil Defence Department, confirmed that the fire had been brought under control.

Shaheen Alam, senior station officer at Tongi Fire Station, said firefighters from different stations worked together to tackle the blaze, considering its severity. As the factory building was made of steel, aluminium and glass, bringing the fire under control proved difficult. The rapid burning of different parts of the building posed challenges for firefighters.

Cause of fire remains unclear

Medicines, production equipment and other materials inside the factory were reportedly damaged in the fire. However, the extent of the damage could not be determined immediately. The exact cause of the fire also remained unknown. The factory authorities suspect that an electrical short circuit may have triggered the blaze. Fire Service officials, meanwhile, believe chemicals may have caused the fire.

Shahidul Islam, senior administrative officer of Drug International Limited, told Prothom Alo, “Around 200 workers are employed at our factory. Suddenly, workers noticed smoke coming from the fourth floor and started shouting. The emergency alarm was then sounded. All the workers managed to leave the factory quickly and safely. There are no flammable substances in our factory. Our initial assumption is that the fire may have originated from an electrical short circuit.”

Brigadier General Sultanul Afreen Junaid, director general of the Fire Service and Civil Defence Department, said the exact cause of the fire had not yet been established.

He said, “We suspect the fire may have originated from chemicals on the fourth floor of the factory building. It took nearly four hours to bring the fire under control. We are now carrying out the damping-down operation to extinguish the remaining fire inside. This work will continue throughout Thursday. We have asked the authorities to provide the necessary documents. We are also examining whether they had adequate firefighting arrangements.”

item.title: Saudi Arabia-bound passengers seek alternative routes amid 100 flight disruptions, rising costs
item.description:
Anwar Hossain from Bogura was scheduled to fly to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, for the first time on a work visa on Tuesday. His IndiGo flight was due to depart from Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka at 3:55pm. However, the flight was cancelled.

He waited at the airport until night before going to a relative’s house in Baipail. From Wednesday morning, he tried to contact the agency in Banani from which he had bought his ticket, but could not reach anyone. He was also unable to contact his employer.

Anwar spoke to Prothom Alo over the phone on Wednesday afternoon.

“I waited all day on Tuesday but couldn’t leave. I’ve been calling everyone since this morning, but no one is answering. This is my first time going abroad, and I don’t understand what I’m supposed to do. I don’t even know how I’ll get there now,” he said.

Asked about buying another ticket to join work, Anwar said, “I’ll have to pay again for a new ticket. Where will I get that much money?”

Additional costs for alternative flights

Like Anwar, Zakir Hossain was scheduled to travel to Riyadh on Tuesday. He had returned to Bangladesh on a three-month leave. His Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight was scheduled for 1:10pm on Tuesday.

After the flight was cancelled, he paid an additional Tk 16,000 for a ticket on a flight to Medina scheduled for 10pm on Wednesday.

Speaking to Prothom Alo on Wednesday afternoon at the canopy area of Terminal 2 at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, the passenger from Katiadi in Kishoreganj said, “Biman told me the route had changed, so I would have to pay another Tk 16,000. I paid and got the ticket. I have to get there somehow.”

Zakir works as a labourer at a factory in Riyadh. His leave ended on Tuesday. He said that when he informed his kafeel (employer) about the flight cancellation in Dhaka, the employer told him to travel by an alternative route.

Atiar Rahman and Sujauddin were scheduled to leave for Umrah on an Air Arabia flight at 4:45pm on Wednesday. They could not travel because the flight was cancelled. Their group consists of 40 Umrah pilgrims.

“We arrived in the morning to catch the flight and learned here that it had been cancelled. Now we’ll have to stay at a hotel. That means additional expenses,” Atiar Rahman told Prothom Alo.

During a visit to Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport between 1pm and 5:30pm on Wednesday, this correspondent spoke to more than 15 passengers. Most passengers travelling to Saudi Arabia whose flights had been cancelled came to the airport to check their flight status. Others waited for alternative flights to reach their destinations. Most said they had not known about the cancellations.

The number of waiting passengers was relatively lower on Wednesday than over the previous four days. However, airline staff were not seen following the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh’s (CAAB) instructions to assist stranded passengers. Travellers were left waiting at the airport on their own. CAAB had sent a letter to airlines on Monday instructing them to keep track of the situation of passengers awaiting flights.

Passengers to Riyadh and Jeddah seeking alternative flights

As of Wednesday afternoon, passengers from some cancelled flights were trying to travel to Saudi Arabia on alternative flights. Before Sunday, some passengers had travelled via Jeddah and Dammam. However, neither CAAB nor Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport authorities could confirm the number of passengers who had done so.

Following an attack on Riyadh airport on Saturday night, flight from Dhaka to Riyadh were cancelled. From Wednesday, some flights to Jeddah and Dammam were also cancelled, according to Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport authorities. A flight to Abu Dhabi was also cancelled on Tuesday.

The airport’s flight information display showed that the 5:30pm Flynas flight to Jeddah had been cancelled.

Passengers wait at Balaka for alternative tickets

Biman Bangladesh Airlines has cancelled its flights to Riyadh and Dammam until 17 October. The state-owned carrier is currently operating flights to Jeddah and Medina. Passengers whose flights have been cancelled are seeking alternative routes to Saudi Arabia.

At Biman’s Balaka office near Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport on Wednesday afternoon, passengers were seen waiting to change their tickets.

Kabir Abdul Hai, a Riyadh-bound passenger from Kaliakair in Gazipur who had come to Balaka to change his ticket, told Prothom Alo, “My Biman flight to Riyadh was scheduled for midnight on Wednesday, but it was cancelled. So now I’m trying to travel via Jeddah. It would be good if I could get a flight to Jeddah.”

He has to return to work after his leave ends on Thursday.

100 flights disrupted, 15,393 passengers affected

Operational restrictions at Saudi Arabian airports have disrupted 100 flights operating between Bangladesh and other destinations through direct and transit routes. Some flights were cancelled while others were suspended. A total of 15,393 passengers have been affected. Of the disrupted flights, 41 were direct flights and 59 were transit flights.

According to a CAAB press release issued on Wednesday evening, the affected direct flights included 17 operated by Biman Bangladesh Airlines, 10 by US-Bangla Airlines, seven by Saudia and seven by Riyadh Air.

Among transit flights, 22 IndiGo flights, 14 Emirates flights, seven SalamAir flights, seven Qatar Airways flights, six flydubai flights, two Air India flights and one EgyptAir flight were affected.

Operations at Saudi Arabian airports have been disrupted following an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. The disruption has also affected flights from Dhaka to Saudi Arabia. Earlier, CAAB had reported cancellations and suspensions as well as disruptions to transit flights.

Amid the situation, Biman Bangladesh Airlines, the national flag carrier, has announced the suspension of all flights from Dhaka to Riyadh and Dammam until 17 October. Meanwhile, private carrier US-Bangla Airlines has cancelled all flights on the Dhaka–Riyadh–Dhaka route until 21 October.

item.title: CUET VC says he has not resigned; teachers and students vow to continue protest
item.description:
Vice-Chancellor of Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET), Professor Sheikh Shariful Alam, has announced that he will resume his duties at the university once he recovers.

He stated that the news being circulated in various media about his resignation is not true. The claim that students allowed him to exit on the condition that he would not return to the campus is also false.

This statement was given by the Vice-Chancellor today, Wednesday afternoon, through a WhatsApp message to Prothom Alo.

After being confined in his office for about 30 hours due to a student movement, he was rescued last Tuesday evening around 6:30 PM by the Chattogram Deputy Commissioner and Superintendent of Police. He is currently admitted to Chittagong Medical College Hospital for treatment, he informed.

Earlier last Monday morning, the Vice-Chancellor Sheikh Shariful Alam entered his office by breaking the lock with the leaders of the Chhatra Dal. Then around 12: 30 PM, students locked the main gate again, keeping him inside. Water and electricity connections were also cut off.

On 21 September, Professor Sheikh Shariful Alam was appointed as Vice-Chancellor of CUET, replacing Professor Abu Sadat Muhammad Sayem.

Protesting this decision, students have been observing a ‘complete shutdown’ programme since 22 September. The university's teachers, officers, and employees have also been on strike demanding the same.

This has halted most academic activities, including classes and exams.
Amidst the protest, on Monday morning, Vice-Chancellor Sheikh Shariful Alam entered his office by breaking the lock with the leaders of the student organisation. Then around 12:30 PM, students locked the main gate again, keeping him inside. Water and electricity connections were also cut off.

What the Vice-Chancellor said:

Vice-Chancellor Sheikh Shariful Alam said, “False news is being spread in various media that I have resigned and will never set foot on the CUET campus in the future. I did not make any such statement or give any speech. As you know, when I was being taken away, I was not in a state to speak. I left the campus due to illness. I am still unwell and under close observation by doctors. Once I recover, I will resume my duties at the university, God willing.”

The Vice-Chancellor further stated, “I want to reiterate that I have come to Chittagong to fulfill the responsibilities entrusted to me by the state. I am not here for personal interests, to implement any specific agenda, or for any party or interest-related purpose. Performing university duties and keeping institutional activities functional are important to me.”

Sheikh Shariful Alam mentioned that he does not want any interest group’s instigation or usage to harm the valuable academic lives and activities of the students. He urged students to return to their classes promptly.

The Teachers' ''Complete Non-cooperation'' Programme to Continue:

The CUET Teachers' Association has stated that their work stoppage and ‘complete non-cooperation’ programme will continue. A general meeting of the Teachers' Association was held today, Wednesday at noon in the university's central auditorium.

After the meeting, CUET Teachers' Association Joint Secretary Samiun Basir said, “We are concerned about the incident of breaking into the Vice-Chancellor's residence. There are important documents inside the building. It needs to be investigated whether they have been stolen and the extent of the damage. We remain firm in our demand to reinstate Professor Sayem as Vice-Chancellor. We will continue the strike and non-cooperation.”

Shutdown to continue:

The students have stated that their ‘complete shutdown’ programme will continue with the demand to reinstate Professor Abu Sadat Muhammad Sayem as Vice-Chancellor. Md Jahangir Alam, a third-year student from the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering and one of the protesting students, told Prothom Alo, “We have been protesting with the demand to reinstate Professor Sayem as Vice-Chancellor. This movement will continue. The shutdown program will remain ongoing with the demand to reinstate Sayem Sir."

The protest by teachers, students, officers, and employees has been ongoing for 23 consecutive days on the CUET campus. This has halted all academic activities, including classes and exams. Meanwhile, many students have started leaving the campus for the Durga Puja holiday. On Wednesday morning, it was observed on-site that a few students were heading home with bags.

item.title: 14 rescued whistling ducks return to nature
item.description: Having bought lesser whistling ducks from a village, poultry vendor Mohammad Rafiqul was roaming through the town hoping to sell them. Suddenly, the caged birds caught the eyes of local bird lovers. Members of the Nature and Wildlife Conservation Community (a voluntary organisation long active in Pabna in environmental and wildlife protection) quickly intervened and made the vendor aware of the wildlife laws. Pledging that he would never trade in wild birds again and would release them at once, the vendor joined the volunteers to set the ducks free in the lake of the Pabna University of Science and Technology (PUST) campus. Exhausted and frail from captivity, the birds briefly splashed in the waters in newfound joy before drifting into a quiet rest with their eyes closed. As dusk descended, the flock rose into the sky in unison, flying away toward safe shelter. Here is a photo story capturing the rescue and release of these 14 lesser whistling ducks.

item.title: 89 flights cancelled in four days, over 14,500 passengers stranded
item.description:
A total of 89 flights have been cancelled over the past four days amid continued Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, leaving more than 14,500 passengers stranded as of Wednesday afternoon.
Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB) spokesperson Kawsar Mahmud shared the information on Wednesday afternoon.
He said 39 direct flights had been cancelled, including 17 operated by Biman Bangladesh Airlines, 10 by US-Bangla Airlines, five by Saudia and seven by Riyadh Air.
Another 50 transit flights were cancelled, including 22 operated by IndiGo, four by SalamAir, one by EgyptAir, 11 by Emirates, six by Qatar Airways and six by flydubai.
Kawser said flight cancellations would continue if the situation did not return to normal.

item.title: PM meets three exemplary people for their contributions to society
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Wednesday met three inspiring individuals who have set remarkable examples in society through their dedication to education, overcoming physical challenges and planting trees.
The three are Nayla Sharaf, a BUET graduate who chose to teach at a primary school, Md Altaf Hossain, who established a school despite having no hands, and Rezaul Kibria Babul, who has planted thousands of trees on his own initiative.
They met the prime minister at his office at the Bangladesh Secretariat and became emotional at the opportunity to meet him.
Tarique listened attentively to their life struggles and initiatives for public welfare, praised their contributions and assured them of necessary support.
“People like you are greatly needed to build the country. Nation-building will become easier if everyone comes forward like you,” he said.
Nayla Sharaf completed her studies at the Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET) and joined the Local Government Engineering Department (LGED) as an assistant engineer. She later worked as an officer at Janata Bank.
Despite qualifying for the 34th Bangladesh Civil Service (BCS) examination, she chose not to join a government job and instead pursued teaching.
For the past seven years, she has been teaching at Panchananpur Government Primary School in Netrokona. She also develops teaching materials and digital content to make learning easier, particularly for disadvantaged children.
Another person who met the prime minister was Md Altaf Hossain of Narsingdi, who was born without both hands.
He learned to write with his feet and established Protiba Dukhu Mia Kindergarten School in Panchdona, Narsingdi, in 2007.
Using his savings and money from the sale of ancestral land, he built the school, which now has 145 students and 10 teachers.
He continues to write with his feet and manages various school activities despite his physical challenges.
After hearing his story, the prime minister assured him of support to construct a new school building.
Rezaul Kibria Babul of Charfasson in Bhola has also set an example through his long-standing efforts to plant trees.
Alongside his work as a mosque imam, he has spent nearly three decades planting thousands of trees along roads with his own money and labour.
After selling ancestral property to establish a nursery, he began planting saplings grown there in different areas. Many of the trees have now grown large enough to provide shade for passers-by.
The prime minister praised all three for their efforts, saying individual initiatives for the welfare of society and the country play an important role and can inspire others to undertake similar work.
He encouraged them to continue their activities and assured them of support.

item.title: 20 Bangladeshis killed in Russia-Ukraine war after 21 days of training
item.description:
Thirty Bangladeshis were allegedly trafficked to Russia on the promise of construction jobs but were instead handed over to the Russian army and sent to the Russia-Ukraine battlefield after just 21 days of military training.
At least 20 of them have reportedly been killed in drone attacks, according to a preliminary investigation by the Special Response Battalion (SRB).
The SRB’s preliminary investigation suggests the Bangladeshis were sent to the battlefield as bait to help identify enemy positions, with drone strikes enabling Russian forces to determine the attackers’ locations.
SRB-10 Battalion Commander Mohammad Asaduzzaman shared the findings at a press conference in Karwan Bazar, Dhaka, on Wednesday.
In connection with the incident, police arrested Mizanur Rahman, 55, founder of Jabal-e-Noor International, and Abu Taher, alias Lentu. The SRB identified them as key figures in the alleged human trafficking network.
According to the SRB, the 30 Bangladeshis travelled to Russia on May 7 through three organisations: Jabal-e-Noor, RS International and TS Group. Each was reportedly charged an average of Tk10 lakh on the promise of construction work.
However, after arriving in Russia, they were allegedly denied the promised jobs and handed over to the Russian army. They were sent to the battlefield after 21 days of training.
“Those who were taken from Bangladesh were not really qualified for war. They had no physical conditioning, training or tactical practice of any kind. So why were they sent after only 21 days of training?” Asaduzzaman said.
He added: “What we have understood is that they were sent to the battlefield as a kind of bait, to identify the enemy’s positions. When the enemy launches drone attacks on them, that country identifies the enemy’s location.”
The SRB said the Bangladeshis were deployed in three groups — front, middle and rear. Seventeen reportedly died in drone attacks on the first day, while three more deaths were reported later. The battalion has preliminarily confirmed the deaths of 20 of the 30 Bangladeshis.
Of the survivors, two have returned to Bangladesh with injuries, Asaduzzaman said. One of them, identified as Rajan, reportedly suffered a broken waist and paralysis of his lower body in a drone strike. He dragged himself on his chest for about four kilometres to reach a camp.
Two others are receiving treatment at a hospital in Moscow, while the remaining six are still on the battlefield, according to the SRB.
Asaduzzaman said a Russian national named Igor and a Kyrgyzstani woman named Julia were also allegedly involved in the trafficking network. Authorities are gathering information about them and conducting operations, while efforts are underway to arrest another alleged member, Mostafizur.
He added that preliminary findings suggest people from several countries have been drawn into the war through similar means.
The Bangladeshis came from various districts, including Gopalganj, Mymensingh, Narayanganj, Jamalpur, Pabna, Chapainawabganj, Faridpur, Rajbari and Gazipur.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,177 as seven die in 24 hours
item.description:
Seven more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Wednesday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,177.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all seven of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,073, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 104, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the seven new suspected fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in Dhaka, with five deaths reported in both the Dhaka division and Dhaka district.
A total of 1,199 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Wednesday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 208,570.
During the same period, 128 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 22,840.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 185,390 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 177,698 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Fire at Drug International factory brought under control in Tongi
item.description:
The fire at Drug International's pharmaceutical factory in Tongi, Gazipur, was brought under control at 1:35pm on Wednesday after 20 Fire Service units joined a multi-agency operation to contain the blaze.
The operation involved the army, Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), police and members of Gazipur City Corporation, alongside the Fire Service.
Fire Service Director General Brigadier General Sultanul Afrain Zunaid disclosed the information at a press briefing at the scene at 2:10pm on Wednesday.
Sultanul Afrain Zunaid said firefighting operations began on an urgent basis under the prime minister's instructions. Although the fire was brought under control at 1:35pm through the efforts of 20 Fire Service units, more time would be needed to extinguish it completely.
The fire broke out on the 4th and 2nd floors of the factory's 7-storey building. The blaze affected emergency medicines, including injections, causing breathing difficulties. No casualties were reported, but a Fire Service personnel member suffered breathing difficulties, and arrangements were made for his treatment.
He said the factory is located on Squib Road in the Tongi industrial area. The fire originated on the 4th floor of the 7-storey Unit 2 building at around 10:15am on Wednesday.
Factory workers initially tried to extinguish the fire using the factory's own firefighting arrangements. However, as the blaze intensified and the situation went out of control, the Fire Service was notified.
After receiving the information, Fire Service units from Tongi, Savar, Gazipur, Ashulia and Dhaka arrived at the scene. Army personnel, BGB members, police and members of Gazipur City Corporation also worked alongside the Fire Service to bring the blaze under control.
The incident disrupted public transport and normal life within an area of around 2km surrounding the factory.
Drug International Manager Shafiqul Islam Badal said the factory initially attempted to control the fire using its own arrangements. However, the intensity of the blaze made assistance from the Fire Service and other relevant forces necessary.

item.title: Top Indian ‘cockroach’ leaders sent to jail after protest
item.description:
Two leaders of India’s youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) were remanded in custody for five days on Wednesday, as police ratcheted up efforts to clamp down on anti-election commission protests.
CJP activists and opposition parties have defied a security crackdown to demand the resignation of India’s chief election commissioner, accusing the poll body of manipulating voter rolls to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling party.
The commission, which oversees voting in the world’s most populous nation, has denied any wrongdoing.
Delhi Police said CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka, 30, and Saurav Das, 27, were taken into custody for their “alleged repeated attempts to disturb public peace and violate the law.”
At the end of the five-day remand period, they could have their detention extended, be granted bail or be released.
On Tuesday, the pair jumped security barricades to wave the national flag at Jantar Mantar, a decades-old protest site that police have barred people from using.
“Their alleged attempts to instigate others through social media to engage in similar unlawful activities were also taken into consideration,” police added.
Parliamentary opposition leader Rahul Gandhi, from the Congress party, backed the men, who were detained after entering the site.
Jantar Mantar, in the heart of the capital, has been sealed off for days with yellow metal barricades and guarded by security personnel.
Delhi Police said on Monday it had removed the site from the list of designated protest venues.
“Waving the Tricolour at Jantar Mantar in a peaceful protest is not a crime,” Gandhi said in a post on social media. “Jailing youth for it is an act of cowardice.”
The Congress and CJP have both organized protests over the voter roll revision. Gandhi said on Wednesday that “all protests are one.”
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke praised the men, saying they “knew they could be thrown behind bars” but went ahead to wave the national flag.
“They’ve shown the entire country that the only way to stand up to a bully like Modi is to never bow down, no matter the consequences,” he said in a post on social media.
Das has worked as a journalist, while Ranka, an engineer, studied at the prestigious Indian Institute of Technology and the London School of Economics.
Rights advocates and critics say Modi’s government has eroded democratic freedoms during more than a decade in power, citing pressure on journalists, civil society groups and political opponents -- allegations the government rejects.
Human Rights Watch said Wednesday the Indian government must uphold the right of citizens to protest peacefully.
“The Modi government should stop throwing young protesters in jail and instead engage with them to address concerns over the right to vote and fairness of elections,” it said in a statement.
One of the protesters, who gave only her first name, said Wednesday she was taken to a detention center where she was beaten by police.
“They punched me here,” said Atira, pointing to her face at a news conference in Delhi, standing next to Gandhi.
“I begged them to stop, but then they started kicking me in my private parts, lower abdomen, and back. They didn’t consider me as a human.”
AFP could not immediately verify her claim.
Journalists in New Delhi marched on Tuesday to protest the detention of reporters during demonstrations. The Press Club of India said any attacks on journalists doing their jobs were “unacceptable.”
The electoral list revision, which began last year, has led to more than 133 million names being removed from voter rolls, according to media reports. Critics say the exercise has disproportionately affected minorities, particularly Muslims.
Election authorities say the move was intended to eliminate duplicate, deceased and fraudulent entries.
Members of Modi’s Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party have long alleged that large numbers of undocumented Muslim migrants from neighboring Bangladesh have fraudulently entered India’s electoral rolls.
Home Minister Amit Shah, Modi’s powerful right-hand man, dismissed the protests as localized and accused Gandhi of pursuing an “action plan to protect infiltrators.”
“The people of India are not going to fall for your deception,” he said, predicting a “resounding majority” for government in the next general election, due in 2029.

item.title: Southeast Bank holds training on trade-based money laundering
item.description:
Southeast Bank PLC. recently organized a training program on Trade-Based Money Laundering (TBML) aimed at enhancing awareness and strengthening Anti-Money Laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) practices among the bank's employees and banking partners.
Md Mahbub Alam, additional managing director & chief risk officer (CRO) of Southeast Bank PLC, inaugurated the event.

item.title: Al-Arafah Islami Bank signs agreement with United School and College
item.description:
Al-Arafah Islami Bank PLC and United School and College have signed a cash management agreement to make student fee collection easier, safer, and more technology-driven.
Under the agreement, students will be able to pay their educational fees through the bank’s branches and Islamic Wallet.
The agreement was signed by SM Abu Jafar, deputy managing director of Al-Arafah Islami Bank PLC and Abdullah Al Mamun, principal of United School and College on behalf of their respective organizations at a ceremony held at the bank’s head office on Tuesday, October 13.
The agreement will make fee payment more convenient for students and their guardians.
At the same time, United School and College will be able to access fee collection information in real time, enabling faster, more accurate, and more efficient reconciliation of accounts.
The agreement will expand technology-driven financial transactions between the bank and educational institutions.
It is also expected to contribute to the expansion of institutional cash management services and increase the mobilization of low-cost deposits for Al-Arafah Islami Bank PLC.
Among others, Md Aminul Islam Bhuiyan, deputy managing director of the bank, Mohammad Abdul Mobin, senior executive vice president, along with other senior officials from the bank and the educational institution, attended the ceremony.
The agreement is expected to further strengthen the use of digital financial services in the education sector while ensuring greater efficiency, transparency, and dynamism in fee collection and financial management for educational institutions.

item.title: Khasru: US should increase support for Bangladesh amid rising imports
item.description:
Finance Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury has said Bangladesh should receive increased support from the United States in view of improving bilateral relations and the country's growing imports from the US.
He made the remarks while briefing journalists after a meeting with officials of the US Treasury Department in Bangkok on Wednesday.
The meeting discussed debt management, US assistance and overall Bangladesh-US relations, the minister said.
He also held discussions with representatives of the US Export-Import Bank (Exim Bank) and other US agencies involved in providing assistance.
"Bangladesh did not receive much from the United States in the past. But, as Bangladesh-US relations have progressed, we are purchasing several aircraft and importing oil, soybeans and various other products and commodities from the US. Therefore, we should receive additional support from them. They agreed on this. Now, let us see," Amir Khasru said.
The finance minister said the government's economic policy prioritizes reducing dependence on loans and increasing foreign direct investment (FDI) and joint investment.
Amir Khasru said he had held extensive discussions with the US Exim Bank on the issue and hoped that Bangladesh could move forward with this approach.
"The main focus of our economic policy is investment. We want to move away from loans and focus more on direct investment and joint investment," he said.
Highlighting Bangladesh's substantial imports from the United States, the minister said purchases of aircraft, oil, soybeans and other commodities had implications for bilateral trade as well as Bangladesh's external balance of payments.
"We have strongly told them that Bangladesh is importing so much from the United States, and bilateral relations have reached their current stage. If support does not come from the US now, when will it come? The assistance we expect should come now," he said.
Amir Khasru said the relevant US parties agreed with Bangladesh's position. However, he added, the extent and modalities of the expected assistance would become clear in the coming days.

item.title: bKash, Bishwo Shahitto Kendro expand book reading program in Bagerhat and Satkhira
item.description:
